scope: local-only; no AWS writes; not browser Apply/Save/Reload proof

results.summary: The design presents a coherent external-sort pipeline with bounded-memory workers, durable manifests, object storage, and queued parallel stages that satisfy the published large-data sorting scope.

findings.title: External-sort pipeline is well matched to oversized datasets
findings.explanation: The design decomposes the job into bounded run generation followed by bounded k-way merges, which is the right core pattern for sorting data that cannot fit in memory.

findings.title: Custom comparator is preserved through all processing stages
findings.explanation: The coordinator stores the versioned comparator specification, run workers apply it during chunk sorting, and merge workers reuse it unchanged, which avoids semantic drift between passes.

findings.title: Backpressure-aware queues support controlled parallelism
findings.explanation: Separate run-generation and merge-stage queues with bounded consumption give the design a clear way to exploit parallel workers without overwhelming memory or storage.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers durable ingestion, windowed exact aggregation, shard-based ranking materialization, and paged top-K querying for sales/download/rating rankings across daily, weekly, and monthly windows.

findings.title: Strong end-to-end ranking pipeline with durable dedupe and replay
findings.explanation: The design clearly separates event acceptance, durable outbox publication, ordered stream processing, exact aggregate persistence, and query-time materialization. This supports near-real-time ranking while preserving correctness under retries and replay.

findings.title: Query path is purpose-built for top-K access and large result pagination
findings.explanation: The query service validates the ranking dimensions, reads shard-local sorted sets, merges exact candidates, and returns freshness metadata and cursors. That is a coherent fit for efficient top-K reads at scale.

findings.title: Operational visibility spans ingestion, streaming, projection, cache and query health
findings.explanation: The monitoring component covers accepted events, deduplication, outbox age, broker lag, processing checkpoints, aggregate conflicts, cache rebuild progress, and query performance. This is sufficient for the exercise’s observability expectations.

results.summary: The design cleanly supports real-time zone-based surge pricing with validated ingestion, event-time aggregation, versioned price publication, fast quote reads, and audited history, while also addressing fairness, manipulation resistance, and sub-second freshness.

findings.title: Versioned zone snapshots preserve pricing consistency
findings.explanation: The cache and quote path are designed around complete immutable zone-price snapshots, which reduces the risk of mixing price versions and supports consistent in-zone quotes.

findings.title: Freshness and integrity are monitored end to end
findings.explanation: Monitoring covers event-to-price freshness, zone skew, backlog, recovery, fallback use, manipulation signals, and notification lag, which is well aligned with the real-time pricing problem.

results.summary: The design cleanly enforces per-account concurrent screen limits with an authoritative transactional store, idempotent lifecycle handling, and monitoring for drift and failure modes.

findings.title: Authoritative transaction path prevents oversubscription
findings.explanation: The coordinator performs strong reads plus a conditional transaction in the account-authoritative store before issuing a lease, which directly supports the screen-cap enforcement requirement and reduces race-condition risk.

findings.title: Outbox and reconciliation provide robust lifecycle recovery
findings.explanation: Committed lifecycle intents are written atomically, then relayed to a durable bus and reconciled by a worker that handles retries and expiry cleanup idempotently. This is a strong fit for start/stop handling and network-issue recovery.

findings.title: Security boundary is explicit and practical
findings.explanation: TLS termination, JWT validation, signed leases, and avoidance of IP-only device identity establish a clear trust boundary for playback authorization and abuse handling.

results.summary: The design covers ETA calculation, real-time trip sharing, privacy controls, GPS-noise handling, historical traffic reuse, and adaptive battery-aware tracking with a coherent streaming and cache-backed architecture.

findings.title: Adaptive mobile sampling supports battery-efficient tracking
findings.explanation: The mobile app purpose explicitly adjusts sampling based on movement, trip state, and device battery, which is the right control for conserving power without dropping core location-sharing behavior.

findings.title: Map matching and confidence-aware ETA improve accuracy under noisy GPS and traffic changes
findings.explanation: The design combines GPS validation, deduplication, map matching, historical traffic, and confidence-bearing ETA prediction, which is a coherent path to more accurate and dynamically updated ETAs.

results.summary: The design covers core IoC/DI scope end to end: typed registration and resolution, constructor/property injection, lifecycle scopes, cycle detection, generic support, code/file configuration, and concurrent atomic registry updates.

findings.title: Typed generic resolution and provider semantics are consistently preserved
findings.explanation: The design keeps generic service identity intact from registration through resolution and deferred provider use, which directly supports type-safe DI for closed generic types.

findings.title: Atomic registry publication avoids partially applied configuration
findings.explanation: Both code and file inputs normalize into the same binding registry with atomic publication, which is a strong fit for concurrent container access.

findings.title: Lifecycle and cycle handling are separated from activation planning
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates plan caching, cycle detection, and lifetime enforcement, which improves maintainability and reduces accidental singleton/transient confusion.

findings.title: Structured diagnostics cover the main DI failure modes
findings.explanation: Missing bindings, ambiguity, generic constraint failures, injection-site problems, construction exceptions, cycles, and disposed scopes are all represented as actionable errors with context.

results.summary: A cohesive control-plane design that covers provisioning, failover, scaling, health, replication, backup/restore, rolling upgrades, and tenant isolation with quorum-safe workflows and explicit partition handling.

findings.title: Tenant-scoped, idempotent control workflow
findings.explanation: The submission cleanly separates user-facing intent capture from durable execution: commands are validated at the gateway, written as versioned desired-state revisions, emitted through an outbox, and processed idempotently by reconcilers. This is a strong fit for cluster lifecycle operations that must survive retries and partial failures.

findings.title: Partition-aware failover safety
findings.explanation: The failover path uses freshness-aware diagnostics, quorum-backed ownership, and fencing epochs, and it explicitly refuses unsafe promotion when topology information is ambiguous. That is a strong consistency-preserving approach for distributed database recovery.

findings.title: Operational visibility is built into the control plane
findings.explanation: Monitoring is not bolted on as a generic checklist; the design surfaces queue age, lease health, reconciliation lag, replica health, failover outcomes, and metadata pressure through dedicated telemetry paths. This provides useful diagnostics for both operators and automation.

findings.title: Safe backup and restore flow
findings.explanation: Backups are resumable, checksummed, versioned, and tied to tenant authorization, while restores select an explicit snapshot version rather than relying on an ambiguous latest-object read. This is a well-structured recovery path.

results.summary: A coherent flash-distribution design with layered abuse controls, durable FIFO acceptance, and ledger-enforced uniqueness/stock correctness.

findings.title: Durable ledger-centric claim correctness
findings.explanation: The design clearly places final claim authority in the transactional ledger and prevents Redis or retry behavior from altering stock or voucher state.

findings.title: FCFS ordering is explicitly modeled
findings.explanation: The queue is described as preserving immutable server acceptance order, and workers consume that order instead of completion order, which is a strong fit for fairness under burst load.

findings.title: Abuse controls are layered before claim execution
findings.explanation: WAF, gateway validation, JWT auth, and per-user distributed throttling reduce wasted work and improve resilience against bots without relying on a single IP-only check.

results.summary: The design cleanly separates control, transfer, storage, and observability paths, with strong support for resumable large-file downloads over HTTP/FTP, bounded memory use, retries, progress reporting, and bandwidth shaping.

findings.title: Streaming architecture preserves large-file handling
findings.explanation: The design keeps file bytes off the control plane and routes artifact bytes through the verified store and client path, which is the right shape for multi-GB downloads.

findings.title: Resumable transfer flow is well anchored in durable checkpoints
findings.explanation: Range checkpoints, idempotent job creation, and stale-worker rejection give the system a coherent resume story after interruption or redelivery.

findings.title: Protocol and source trust boundaries are explicit
findings.explanation: The worker-to-origin link makes HTTP/FTP handling explicit and treats origin metadata as untrusted, which supports the declared protocol constraint.

results.summary: A highly coherent regulated wire-transfer design with strong idempotency, ACID durability, fraud/compliance gating, status tracking, and auditability across domestic and international paths.

findings.title: End-to-end wire flow is well decomposed
findings.explanation: The submission cleanly separates initiation, validation, compliance, fraud, durable commit, dispatch, reconciliation, and archival concerns, which makes the regulated transfer path easy to reason about and implement.

findings.title: Durable correctness strategy is coherent
findings.explanation: The combination of ACID ledger writes, scoped idempotency, transactional outbox, durable queueing, and reconciliation directly addresses duplicate prevention, crash recovery, and external-rail ambiguity.

findings.title: Security boundaries are consistently applied
findings.explanation: The gateway, auth, encryption, restricted KYC store, scoped secrets management, and audit-aware archive establish clear trust boundaries for sensitive transfer and identity data.

results.summary: The design provides a coherent petabyte-scale migration flow for databases and files with baseline copy, CDC delta sync, validation, monitored cutover, rollback controls, and security controls aligned to the stated constraints.

A coherent enterprise RAG platform with bounded context, authorized hybrid retrieval, grounded generation, feedback capture, and monitoring; the design is well matched to the published core scope and constraints.

findings.title: Evidence-only answer path and citation validation are well aligned with grounded responses
findings.explanation: The orchestrator passes only authorized evidence into the LLM, and the guardrails validate citation IDs and citation-to-claim support before any user-visible response. This directly supports the cited-response requirement and reduces hallucination risk.

findings.title: Hybrid dense + sparse retrieval with reranking is a strong retrieval strategy
findings.explanation: Running filtered vector search and BM25 in parallel, then fusing and reranking candidates, is a solid approach for enterprise knowledge retrieval where exact terms and semantic matches both matter.
